_meta.description: Competitive intelligence on SCF/WC platform vendors — sourced from direct website visits (May 2026). Distinguishes white-label-to-banks from direct-to-corporate SaaS, which is the critical axis for CredAble positioning.
_meta.research_method: Direct website scraping of vendor product pages (May 2026) + historical press records. NOT training-data inference.
_meta.key_axis: WHITE-LABEL (bank resells vendor platform under own brand) vs DIRECT-SaaS (vendor sells direct to corporates, banks are funders only)

white_label_competitors._note: These directly compete with CredAble's core model: they sell technology infrastructure TO BANKS who then deploy to corporates under their own brand.

platforms.name: FIS Supply Chain Finance Suite (formerly Demica)
platforms.acquisition_history: Demica acquired by FIS Global (acquired ~2022); legacy Demica Finance Limited FCA-authorized entity maintained (FRN 728209)
platforms.white_label_verbatim: Enables financial institutions to 'act as a single source for comprehensive supply chain finance solutions by streamlining operations.' Banks deliver complete SCF products while leveraging third-party technology providers.
platforms.target_customers: Banks and financial institutions (primary), Corporate CFOs (secondary via bank)
platforms.credable_notes: Most direct competitor. Same model: white-label SCF platform to banks. FIS distribution advantage (installed in many bank cores). CredAble differentiator: faster deployment, TCI integration, Finastra synergy.

platforms.name: Kyriba
platforms.white_label_verbatim: Website lists 'Banks' under 'By Business' with explicit link to white-label solution page. Confirmed SaaS architecture.
products: White-label for Banks (specific product page confirmed)
platforms.credable_notes: Primarily treasury / TMS focused; SCF is a secondary product. White-label confirmed but core strength is treasury, not SCF depth. CredAble advantage: deeper SCF/TF product breadth, TCI integration.

platforms.name: Trade Ledger
platforms.white_label_verbatim: Banks implement Trade Ledger as end-to-end digital business credit management platform. Named bank clients: Barclays, HSBC.
products: Working Capital Lending (99% of products supported)
platforms.delivery_model: Composable SaaS, API + event-based architecture, AWS/Azure
platforms.target_customers: Banks (primary) — sold to FIs who deploy to business borrowers
platforms.credable_notes: Strong in lending origination (LOS) — overlaps CredAble's LOS product. Weaker on structured trade, TCI integration, Flash Title. CredAble advantage: broader SCF product suite, TCI integration.

direct_to_corporate_saas._note: These sell DIRECTLY to corporates (buyers/anchors). Banks participate as funders/liquidity providers only, with NO white-label branding. Different competitive dynamic: CredAble must position vs these at the bank level (bank's own program vs bank-backed fintech program).

platforms.name: Taulia (SAP)
platforms.white_label_verbatim: Website presents Taulia as direct service provider. No white-label offering to banks described. Banks participate as funding providers to Taulia-branded programs only.
platforms.delivery_model: Cloud SaaS, SAP-integrated (SAP ERP / S4/HANA native)
platforms.target_customers: Large corporates and enterprises (Airbus, T-Mobile, REWE, Saudi Aramco cited)
platforms.bank_role: Funding providers only — banks provide liquidity but Taulia is the branded platform
platforms.credable_notes: Not a white-label threat to CredAble's bank business. Taulia competes at the ANCHOR level — if a bank's corporate client already uses Taulia, the bank loses the program to Taulia's branded platform. CredAble pitch: bank keeps program ownership, relationship, and revenue vs delegating to Taulia.
platforms.post_greensill_context: Post-SAP acquisition (2022), Taulia expanded aggressively into corporate SCF — but as DIRECT provider, NOT as bank white-label. Banks using Taulia lose program control.

platforms.name: C2FO
platforms.white_label_verbatim: Platform presented as marketplace. No bank white-label described.
products: C2FO Early Pay (early payment on approved invoices)
platforms.target_customers: Large enterprises and their supplier networks
platforms.bank_role: Third-party lenders via 'Lending Connections' — not platform partners
platforms.credable_notes: Marketplace model. Banks are peripheral. CredAble's bank-owned program model is structurally different.

platforms.name: PrimeRevenue
platforms.white_label_verbatim: No white-label bank program described. Mentions 'Funding Network' but structure unclear.
platforms.delivery_model: Centralized SaaS platform (Supply Chain Financial Portal)
platforms.target_customers: 30,000+ clients in 90+ countries — buyer + supplier sides
platforms.credable_notes: SCF-focused but operates as neutral marketplace. Banks are funders. CredAble pitch: bank owns the program vs feeding PrimeRevenue's network.

platforms.name: Orbian
platforms.white_label_verbatim: Uses 'proprietary Bank Pool funding structure' — banks fund Orbian programs but Orbian is branded. No white-label model to banks.
products: Supply Chain Finance (buyers pay Orbian back; Orbian pays suppliers early)
Payment with Terms (buyers get extended terms; suppliers paid on due date)
platforms.bank_role: Bank Pool funders — competitive, anonymous funding via trustee
platforms.credable_notes: Focused exclusively on largest global corporates (Fortune 500). Not competing in mid-market bank-white-label space.

bank_consortia_and_infra._note: These provide infrastructure TO banks — documentary trade, network connectivity, KYC. Not SCF white-label per se but relevant for CredAble's documentary trade products.

platforms.name: komgo
platforms.notable_2025: MUFG, ING Deutschland, Standard Chartered integrations 2025; acquired GlobalTrade Corporation
platforms.credable_notes: Focused on trade documentation and KYC, not SCF/working-capital white-label. Complementary rather than competitive.

platforms.name: Surecomp (RIVO)
platforms.delivery_model: Cloud SaaS or on-premise, AWS, ISO 27001, SOC 2, SWIFT certified
platforms.credable_notes: Trade finance ops platform. Overlaps on documentary trade but not SCF/WC white-label at same scope.

platforms.name: Tradeshift / Semfi by HSBC
platforms.white_label_verbatim: Tradeshift established JV with HSBC ('Semfi by HSBC') — HSBC-specific, not a general bank white-label offering.
platforms.delivery_model: Enterprise SaaS, e-invoicing + AP automation focus
platforms.target_customers: Large enterprises (Air France, Schaeffler, Société Générale, DHL cited)
platforms.notable: HSBC majority stake JV 'Semfi by HSBC' announced Feb 2024
platforms.credable_notes: Primarily AP/e-invoicing automation. SCF via embedded HSBC funding. Not a general white-label bank platform. HSBC is effectively removed from prospect pool via this JV.

defunct_historical._note: Collapsed or pivoted platforms. Historical context for the Replacement Gap pitch argument.

platforms.name: Greensill Capital
platforms.notes: Supply chain finance lender, balance-sheet model with insurance backing. Collapsed when Tokio Marine withdrew insurance cover. USD 10bn Credit Suisse SCF funds frozen. 3-4 year gap in market.
platforms.credable_implication: THE primary pitch argument — the Replacement Gap. Banks that lost SCF programs waited 3-4 years for market to consolidate.

platforms.name: we.trade
platforms.notes: Blockchain-based open account trade platform. Failed to achieve corporate adoption. 12 founding banks lost JV investment.
platforms.credable_implication: Banks now skeptical of blockchain/consortium SCF — more receptive to proven white-label alternatives. KBC still seeking replacement.

platforms.name: Marco Polo Network
platforms.notes: Blockchain trade finance network. Filed for insolvency after burning through VC funding.
platforms.credable_implication: Commerzbank and others orphaned for documentary trade tech.

platforms.name: FundThrough
platforms.notes: Pivoted from B2B bank partnerships to direct invoice factoring for SMEs. Reduced white-label competition.
platforms.credable_implication: Smaller pool of bank white-label competitors post-pivot.

jpmorgan_clarification.name: JPMorgan Chase
jpmorgan_clarification.status: NOT currently in SCF white-label or SCF-as-a-service business
jpmorgan_clarification.source: User correction (David Perron, May 2026): 'JPMorgan n'est plus dans ce business'
jpmorgan_clarification.historical_context: JPMorgan had participated in some post-Greensill corporate SCF programs 2024-2025 as a direct bank funder (not white-label provider). They serve their own corporate clients with bespoke treasury/working capital solutions but are NOT a platform vendor or white-label SCF provider.
jpmorgan_clarification.action_taken: Removed 'jpmorgan scf' from MAJOR_COMPETITOR_PLATFORMS in extraction_schema.js. Corrected fintech_failures.json Greensill entry.
jpmorgan_clarification.current_scf_products: JPMorgan offers SCF to their own corporate banking clients as part of their wholesale banking suite — but this is proprietary bank lending, not a white-label technology platform.

credable_differentiation.vs_fis_demica: CredAble: faster deployment (3-6 months vs longer), TCI integration native, Finastra pre-integration, Flash Title/TradeCo Hub model
credable_differentiation.vs_kyriba: CredAble: deeper SCF product breadth, not treasury-centric, stronger in emerging markets
credable_differentiation.vs_taulia: CredAble: bank OWNS the program (vs Taulia takes program ownership). Bank keeps P&L, relationship, data.
credable_differentiation.vs_primerevenue_c2fo: CredAble: bank-branded, bank-controlled, not a neutral marketplace
credable_differentiation.vs_trade_ledger: CredAble: broader product suite (SCF + receivables + TCI + Flash Title), not lending-only
